item.title: TT-104: Undo
item.brief:
Implement ticket TT-104 from BACKLOG.md in the repo root, following its acceptance criteria exactly. Module: tasktracker/store.py (class TaskStore with add, complete, delete; add undo()). Acceptance criteria (verbatim from BACKLOG.md):
- It reverts the most recent not-yet-undone add, complete or delete; repeated calls walk further back (LIFO), across all three kinds.
- Undoing an add removes that task; undoing a complete makes the task open again; undoing a delete restores the task exactly as it was, under the same id.
- Ids are never reused, even after undoing an add.
- With nothing left to undo, undo() raises NothingToUndo (defined in tasktracker.store).
- Failed operations (e.g. completing an unknown id) are not recorded.
Constraints: standard library only; keep existing tests passing with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`; add unit tests for what you build in tests/; keep functions under 60 lines and follow the existing code style. Do not change other tickets' areas. Commit only this ticket's work as one commit on the local branch.

state.summary:
TT-104 undo is implemented and committed as 3f4aa35 on archon/xsmt1k1v-tt-104-undo (on top of base 0a14101). Only tasktracker/store.py and tests/test_store_undo.py changed.

What changed: TaskStore keeps an in-memory undo log. add, complete and delete append an entry only after they succeed, so failed calls (blank title, unknown id) are not recorded. undo() pops the newest entry and reverses it: add removes the task, complete restores the previous status, delete puts the same Task object back under its id. Ids are never reused because _next_id is not rolled back. With an empty log undo() raises NothingToUndo, defined in tasktracker.store.

pr.body:
Approach: TaskStore keeps an in-memory _undo_log of tuples. add, complete and delete append an entry only after they succeed, so failed calls are not recorded. undo() pops the last entry and dispatches to _undo_add, _undo_complete or _undo_delete. complete records the previous status; delete records the removed Task object and restores it under the same id. Ids are not rolled back.

Key files: tasktracker/store.py (undo log, undo and its helpers, NothingToUndo), tests/test_store_undo.py (9 tests covering each kind, LIFO across kinds, exact restore, empty-log error, no id reuse, and failed operations not recorded).

Checks: unit tests 13 OK; py_compile OK; pyflakes not installed.

Assumptions and limits: undo state is in memory only and is not persisted. Completing an already-done task is recorded, and undoing it is a no-op (non-blocking follow-up). Invariants use assert, which python -O removes (non-blocking follow-up).
pr.summary: Made undo() possible on TaskStore. now can revert the latest add, complete or delete, LIFO, with NothingToUndo when empty. before: no undo, now: undo() reverses successful operations and never reuses ids.

No concurrency, persistence or external I/O. Tests: 9 new unit tests, all 13 pass. Review: no blocking findings; the reviewer confirmed medium.

item.title: TT-103: Search query syntax
item.brief:
Implement ticket TT-103 from BACKLOG.md in the repo root, following its acceptance criteria exactly. Module: tasktracker/search.py (function search(tasks, query)). Acceptance criteria (verbatim from BACKLOG.md):
- The query is split into terms on whitespace, except inside double quotes: "fix login" is one phrase term. All terms must match (AND).
- A bare word or phrase matches when it appears in the title, case-insensitively.
- tag:NAME matches tasks that have the tag NAME (exact tag, case-insensitive).
- status:open / status:done match on status.
- Any other field:value term, an unknown status, or an unterminated quote raises QueryError (defined in tasktracker.search).
- An empty or blank query matches every task. Results keep the input order.
Constraints: standard library only; keep existing tests passing with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`; add unit tests for what you build in tests/; keep functions under 60 lines and follow the existing code style. Do not change other tickets' areas. Commit only this ticket's work as one commit on the local branch.

item.title: TT-102: RFC 4180 CSV export
item.brief:
Implement ticket TT-102 from BACKLOG.md in the repo root, following its acceptance criteria exactly. Module: tasktracker/export.py (function to_csv(tasks)). Acceptance criteria (verbatim from BACKLOG.md):
- to_csv(tasks) joins fields with commas and breaks on titles containing commas, quotes or newlines. It must produce RFC 4180 CSV.
- Header id,title,tags,status,due; one row per task in the given order.
- Tags joined with ;, due date as ISO YYYY-MM-DD or empty.
- A field containing a comma, double quote, CR or LF is wrapped in double quotes, with embedded double quotes doubled. Other fields are not quoted.
- Every line (header included) ends with CRLF.
Constraints: standard library only; keep existing tests passing with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`; add unit tests for what you build in tests/; keep functions under 60 lines and follow the existing code style. Do not change other tickets' areas. Commit only this ticket's work as one commit on the local branch.

item.title: TT-101: Reject impossible due dates
item.brief:
Implement ticket TT-101 from BACKLOG.md in the repo root, following its acceptance criteria exactly. Module: tasktracker/dates.py (function parse_due(text, today)). Acceptance criteria (verbatim from BACKLOG.md):
- An impossible calendar date (2026-02-30, 2025-02-29, 2026-04-31, 2026-13-01, 2026-00-10) raises InvalidDate, a ValueError subclass defined in tasktracker.dates, whose message contains the original text.
- Anything else that does not match a supported form also raises InvalidDate (today it raises a bare ValueError).
- Relative offsets: +Nd is N days after today, +0d is today. Negative or unsigned offsets (-3d, 3d) raise InvalidDate.
- today and tomorrow keep working; matching stays case-insensitive and ignores surrounding whitespace.
Constraints: standard library only; keep existing tests passing with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`; add unit tests for what you build in tests/; keep functions under 60 lines and follow the existing code style. Do not change other tickets' areas. Commit only this ticket's work as one commit on the local branch.
